description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:747-791 — JmapBackend::Error is bound
as `std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static`. The doc comment lays
out an extensive contract that the type's Display impl MUST NOT
include credential material, blob content, or PII shaped like an
email address. The runtime guard `server_fail_from_backend` at
handlers.rs:69-71 ensures the Display output never reaches the JMAP
wire response — but only for the handlers in jmap-server's own
handlers.rs.

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That a third-party backend implementor reads the doc comment.
   The Display contract is hundreds of words of prose, two levels
   deep in trait-associated-type documentation. The first time a
   backend implementor reads it is when they hit the contract
   violation in code review — if ever.

2. That the kit's defense-in-depth covers every leakage path. The
   server_fail_from_backend runtime guard covers handlers.rs but
   not:
   - Extension *-server crates that build their own per-method
     handlers (mail, chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode,
     sharing, metadata — 8 today).
   - Consumer-side `tracing::error!(err = ?backend_err)` logging that
     formats the Display string into operator logs verbatim.
   - Test assertions that print the error for diagnostic purposes
     and end up in CI logs.
   - Any future tracing-instrumented call that interpolates the
     error with `{}` or `{err}` format specifiers.

3. That a future contributor adds a new server-side surface (e.g. a
   metrics path that emits the Display string as a label) without
   re-reading the contract.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is: a backend implementor wraps a
downstream service error (Postgres, S3, Redis) that interpolates the
caller's bearer token into its error text. The kit's
`server_fail_from_backend` strips it from the wire, but the
consumer's structured logger captures it in operator logs because
the contract is doc-only.

Resolution paths (one or more):

- Make the trait bound enforce a marker trait `RedactedError: Display`
  whose `Display` impl is constrained at the type level. Implementors
  derive or hand-write the Display. The bound makes the contract a
  compile-time requirement.

- Type-erase the error at the trait surface: `type Error = Box<dyn
  std::error::Error + Send + Sync>` so consumers never see the
  concrete Display; or `type Error: SafeDisplay` where SafeDisplay
  has a narrower contract.

- Provide a `redact()` helper method on the trait with a default
  impl that returns a static string; backends override only if they
  want to expose more.

- At minimum: ship a workspace-level lint or canary test that
  checks every concrete `JmapBackend::Error` impl produces a Display
  containing none of a set of canary credentials inserted by the
  test harness. The existing pattern (bd:JMAP-sc1b.79, bd:JMAP-sc1b.102)
  is a precedent — extend it to backend errors.

The current contract is a docs-only commitment in a position where
the consumer's incentives are misaligned (rich error info helps
debugging at the cost of accidental leak). Type-level or test-level
enforcement closes that gap.
title: JmapBackend::Error Display contract is doc-only MUST-NOT; no type-level enforcement of credential/blob/PII redaction
